findings.title: Governance conversion admits an undefined raw rational
findings.finding: MeasurementValue::ExactRational(BigRational::new_raw(1,0)) is classified exact and cloned into GovernanceScalar::Exact without denominator validation. Display conversion rejects the same denominator, and neighboring affine/clock owners explicitly validate it. This is a representation-domain gap, not a demonstrated raw-evidence authority escalation.
findings.recommended_action: Canonicalize and reject zero denominators before creating a governance scalar; apply the invariant to public/deserialized exact packets.
findings.validation: RQPR-CHECK001 independent match-arm control; no original Rust execution.

findings.title: Access-control heading overstates declarative records

Its more precise comments acknowledge that no boundary audit checker is implemented. Tests establish membership and labels, not denied imports or runtime reads.

findings.validation: Complete547-line source-body review; no global claim that no enforcement exists elsewhere.

findings.title: Unchecked decimal placeholder silently saturates ordinary inputs
findings.finding: BigDecimal::from_f64_unchecked multiplies by10^18 then casts to i64. Input42 becomes i64::MAX/10^18 (about9.22337), while NaN becomes zero under Rust saturating cast semantics. The function is explicitly unchecked and marked placeholder, but returned decimal carries no indication of lost magnitude.
findings.recommended_action: Keep this placeholder out of evidence-producing callers; replace with a fallible exact binary/decimal conversion and explicit range/precision policy.
findings.validation: RQPR-CHECK002 independent saturation arithmetic; no native execution or governance-bypass claim.

findings.title: McNemar denominator exponent truncates valid u64 counts
findings.finding: For b=2^32,c=0, n=b+c is representable, min(b,c)=0, numerator2 and the denominator2^(n as u32)=1. The implementation clips to p=1; the exact two-sided conditional p is2^(1-2^32). Unchecked n addition can separately wrap or panic. No native execution or enormous BigInt was needed to derive this source counterexample.
findings.recommended_action: Check count addition and exponent representation; introduce explicit work/count limits with typed refusal rather than truncating or accepting impractical exponentiation.
findings.validation: Exact symbolic source substitution only; independent executable control deferred by evaluation priority.

findings.title: Public second marginal helper panics on ragged input
findings.finding: second_marginal takes a raw slice of rows, obtains width from the first row, then indexes every row at each column without shape validation. The two-row input [[1],[]] reaches row[0] on the empty second row. This violates the crate-level no-caller-data-panic aspiration; private instrument admission does not protect this separate public helper.
findings.recommended_action: Accept a validated joint-table carrier or return a typed rectangularity error before indexing.
findings.validation: Complete source-path counterexample; no native execution.

findings.title: Several rational admission boundaries panic before rejecting raw zero denominators
findings.finding: Rational is a public BigRational alias and admits new_raw(1,0). ProbabilityVector::try_new sees is_negative=false then sums this value; num-rational addition divides by the zero denominator or reduces it with an explicit panic. ClassicalInstrument compares it to zero and num-rational Ord reaches division by zero. SignedValuation sums before any validity check. These APIs return Result but do not make malformed rational input a typed refusal. The simplex/marginal owners demonstrate a stronger explicit denominator gate.

dependency_evidence.context: Partial dependency source review only; Cargo.lock pins num-rational 0.4.2, and core_number_theory/src/rational.rs:26 is the alias.

findings.recommended_action: Validate positive/nonzero denominator and canonicalize where appropriate before sign, comparison, sum or quotient operations at every public rational boundary.
findings.validation: Source-level derivation using the locally pinned dependency; no compiled Rust or native failure execution.

findings.title: Zero-step Markov evolution bypasses the chain carrier check
findings.finding: distribution_after clones initial and validates its dimension only by calling step in the loop. For steps=0, a two-state chain returns a three-state ProbabilitySimplex unchanged, while steps=1 rejects that same input. The declared output law p P^steps is therefore not on the chain carrier for this admitted branch.
findings.recommended_action: Validate initial.n against self.n before the zero-step branch; add a mismatched-carrier zero-step regression.
findings.validation: Exact control-flow substitution; existing source test covers only a matching zero-step carrier. No native replay.

findings.title: Selected residual minima have the wrong stated distance-bound direction
findings.finding: min_weight_nontrivial describes its selected-list minimum as a proxy for a distance lower bound. Even when every supplied vector really is closed and nontrivial, minimizing over a subset yields an upper bound on the full minimum. For d0=0,d1=0 on F2^3, true nontrivial quotient distance is 1; supplying only [1,1,1] returns 3, whose inferred radius would be 1 instead of the true guaranteed radius 0. The helper also does not itself check closedness or quotient nontriviality.
findings.recommended_action: Describe the returned quantity as a selected-candidate minimum; only use it as a distance lower bound after a separate exhaustive or proved exclusion of all smaller nontrivial classes. Keep the supplied distance premise explicit.
findings.validation: Independent exhaustive enumeration of the seven nonzero binary words of length three; no original Rust execution.

findings.title: Public GF2 matrix data bypasses classifier admission
findings.finding: GF2Matrix has public rows/cols/data and derives Deserialize. from_data normalizes entries, but raw construction/deserialization bypasses it. RREF pivots only on literal 1 while other paths use parity. With raw d0=[[3]], shape1x1, d1=zeros(0,1), omega=[1], the classifier computes rank(d0)=0, normalized augmented rank=1 and emits ClosedResidual with q1_dimension=1. Modulo-two semantics give d0=[[1]], so omega is Exact and quotient dimension0. Raw inconsistent row lengths additionally reach unchecked indexing in matmul/rref/apply_d1 rather than a typed refusal.
findings.recommended_action: Make representation private with validated deserialization, or validate/normalize dimensions and binary entries at every public computation boundary. Add malformed-deserialization and nonbinary-raw regression cases.
findings.validation: Exact independent reconstruction of the one-column pivot/augmentation counterexample; native panic paths are source-derived, not executed.

findings.title: Single-row periodic grids mishandle self-loop incidence
findings.finding: try_surface_grid admits m,n>=1. build_surface_d0 assigns1 to both endpoints instead of XORing endpoint incidences. When a periodic extent is1, those endpoints coincide and a loop is incorrectly given a nonzero coboundary row. For m=1,n=2, the returned d1*d0 has rows[1,1], so the supposed complex is not boundary-valid. For1x1 it passes d1*d0=0 but has quotient dimension1 rather than2 for the declared torus.
findings.recommended_action: XOR endpoint incidences so self-loops cancel, or explicitly refuse periodic extents below2. Validate the returned chain condition and test1x1,1x2,2x1 cases; retain checks for normal2x2 grids.
findings.validation: Independent exact finite incidence reconstruction, no native execution.

findings.title: Noise simulation accepts invalid Bernoulli parameters
findings.finding: noise_mc_planar_grid validates m and trials but not p. Lcg::bernoulli returns false for p<=0 and true for p>=1, while the receipt retains the supplied p and labels the run IID Bernoulli(p). Thus p=-1 and p=2 produce accepted diagnostic receipts for nonexistent probability models instead of typed refusals. Nonfinite inputs are also not rejected at admission.
findings.recommended_action: Require finite0<=p<=1 at the public simulation boundary and describe the discrete pseudorandom threshold approximation explicitly. Add out-of-range and nonfinite parameter regressions.
findings.validation: Exact control-flow substitution at p=-1 and p=2; no original Rust execution.

findings.title: Caller-supplied defect weight can hide a capacity-wall label
findings.finding: DefectEvent exposes residual and weight independently. terminalize_packet classifies residual but passes the stored weight to classify_wall_terminal and copies it to the receipt. For the torus logical residual of true Hamming weight2 and declared distance2 (radius0), the complete constructor yields CapacityWallHit; constructing the same public packet with weight0 retains ClosedResidual and reports residual_weight0. The quotient classification is unchanged, but the capacity decision and receipt weight are no longer bound to the residual.
findings.recommended_action: Recompute the weight from the admitted GF(2) residual, or reject a supplied weight mismatch. Add a regression comparing constructor-generated and directly deserialized packets.
findings.validation: Independent exact branch substitution and existing fully read torus fixture/classifier definitions; no native execution.
